self_conditional_modifiers_json.description: R1 Rondo of Slumber: performing healing grants Vatsamonga's Vatic Vintage (10s, max 3 stacks, works off-field): +4% Max HP per stack on the wielder, and while a nearby party member has triggered Frozen or Stellar Swirl in the last 5s the boost is 75% larger (+7% per stack). The +4% Healing Bonus is not modelled. The same stacks also raise the ACTIVE character's ATK off the wielder's HP -- that half is the others-scope vaticVintageActiveAtk* inputs (a wielder that is itself the scored on-field character would need an ATK%-from-HP-excess conversion that does not exist; her own ATK barely matters on an HP scaler). R2-R5 in refinementStates.

others_conditional_modifiers_json.description: R1 Rondo of Slumber, others scope, 3 stacks assumed (a healer that heals every few seconds keeps them up): the currently active party member's ATK is increased by 0.4% per stack for every 1,000 Max HP the WIELDER has over 40,000, capped at 8% per stack -- i.e. 1.2% per 1,000 HP over 40,000, capped at +24% at 60,000 HP. Type the wielder's Max HP; blank assumes 50,000 (= +12% ATK). R1 rate only: at R5 the rate and cap double, which this input cannot express -- scale by hand or pick R1. Use the *ReactionBoosted twin instead when Frozen / Stellar Swirl keeps the +75% up.

R1 Rondo of Slumber, others scope, 3 stacks with the Frozen / Stellar Swirl +75% boost up for the whole rotation: the active character's ATK is increased by 2.1% per 1,000 Max HP the WIELDER has over 40,000, capped at +42%. Type the wielder's Max HP; blank assumes 50,000 (= +21% ATK). R1 rate only. Exclusive with vaticVintageActiveAtk.

source.note: 7.1 weapon, added 2026-09-22 (release day) from nanoka 7.1 data; neither Amber nor GO carry it yet. Base stats derived as init x levels['90'] + last ascension add (the derivation validated against the existing seed files for the 7.0 batch). Buffs baked at R1 (house convention: 4* at R5, 5* at R1, higher tiers in refinementStates). Vodyanitsa's signature. The ATK cap reads as per stack (0.4%/1,000 -> 8% at 60,000 HP), so 3 stacks cap at 24%; if it turns out to be a total cap, halve the caps here.
